newsitem.title: USA: Citadel women cadets transfer to state school.
newsitem.headline: Citadel women cadets transfer to state school.

text.p: Two female cadets who left The Citadel this week because of an alleged hazing incident have transferred to the University of South Carolina, a school official said Wednesday.

Kim Messer and Jeanie Mentavlos, two of the four women who enrolled at The Citadel after it changed its all-male admissions policy last summer, were accepted at USC three days after announcing they would not return to the military college.
"They both have applied to transfer, have been accepted and it is our understanding that they intend to attend this term," USC spokesman Russ McKinney said.
The two women announced Sunday that they would not return to The Citadel, citing safety concerns and broken promises from school officials.

Messer and Mentavlos alleged that nail polish remover was thrown on their clothes by upperclassmen and set afire, and that a cadet made a death threat against them. Neither woman was injured in the alleged incidents, reported in December.
On Monday Maj.-Gen. Clifton Poole, interim president of the school, urged the two to return to classes at The Citadel and conceded that some cadets had "overstepped the bounds of our rules."
The Citadel said last week that 11 cadets had been charged with school violations in the alleged hazing.

The military college began admitting women after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled single-gender education unconstitutional at publicly funded Virgina Military Institute, the only other state-funded all-male military college in the country.
